name: SchemaGrove
author: ScatterSky Development

sections.description:
SchemaGrove turns Schema.org structured data into a visual graph. Connect entities, choose properties, bind values to WordPress content, validate the graph, and preview the exact JSON-LD before saving.

The Lite plugin includes:

  • A visual per-post and per-page schema graph editor.
  • Selectable public WordPress content types, including registered product and custom post types.
  • A full searchable Schema.org type and property catalog generated from the Apache-2.0 schema-dts project, with a reliable built-in fallback.
  • Safe dynamic bindings for post, author, featured-image, date, and site values.
  • Repeated values, first-class nested schemas, connected entity references, graph import/export, and content-aware starter flows.
  • Server-side validation and JSON-LD compilation.
  • A bounded, pannable Site Graph for page hierarchy, links present in stored post content, and saved schema relationships.
  • An optional, resumable setup wizard that explains site identity, schema planning, and publishing ownership in plain language.
  • Resource limits and capability checks for every graph operation.
  • A clean extension surface for a separately distributed Pro add-on.

The separately distributed SchemaGrove Pro add-on supplies agent discoverability analysis, site-wide entity intelligence, conditional templates, operational diagnostics, and automated agent-readiness tooling. SchemaGrove Lite remains fully usable for every function listed above and makes no external AI requests.

Privacy

SchemaGrove Lite stores schema graphs in WordPress post metadata and settings in the WordPress options table. Each saved graph also records its revision, save time, and the WordPress user ID that last edited it for concurrency and audit context. It sends no content or personal data to an external service. Suggested disclosure text is also added to WordPress’s Privacy Policy Guide.

Developer Notes

The authenticated REST namespace is schemagrove/v1. Cookie-authenticated requests use the standard wp_rest nonce; application passwords continue to work through WordPress REST authentication. Human-readable JavaScript and CSS source, pinned build dependencies, and reproducible build instructions are included in src/, package.json, package-lock.json, and README.md. Key extension hooks include schemagrove_allowed_bindings, schemagrove_binding_value, schemagrove_vocabulary_catalog, schemagrove_graph_before_save, schemagrove_graph_validation, schemagrove_effective_graph, schemagrove_compiled_json_ld, schemagrove_should_output, schemagrove_admin_config, schemagrove_is_pro_active, schemagrove_register_rest_routes, and schemagrove_loaded.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the schemagrove directory to /wp-content/plugins/ or install its ZIP from Plugins > Add New.
  2. Activate SchemaGrove.
  3. Follow the optional guided setup, or skip it and open SchemaGrove > Schema Graph directly.
  4. Select a post or page, edit the graph, validate it, preview it, and save.

In Lite, JSON-LD is emitted only for singular content with an explicitly saved, valid graph. When Pro is active, an active conditional template can supply the effective graph; any saved per-post graph is applied last as the override.
sections.faq:
Does SchemaGrove execute values entered in the graph?

No. Dynamic values use a fixed allowlist. Graph data cannot name PHP functions or callbacks.

How do I add nested schema properties?

Select an object-compatible property such as logo, address, author, or offers, then choose Create nested schema in the property inspector. SchemaGrove recommends the compatible Schema.org type, creates and connects the child in one undoable action, and opens its Entity ID field. The canvas displays each level as entity, property, nested entity, and nested property connections, with nesting supported up to the plugin’s safety limit.

Will uninstalling remove my graphs?

Not by default. Enable “Remove data on uninstall” in SchemaGrove settings before uninstalling if you want graph metadata and settings deleted.

Does Lite contact Schema.org or an AI provider?

No. The vocabulary ships with the plugin and compilation happens in WordPress. Add-ons must disclose any external services they introduce.
sections.changelog:
1.0.8

  • Kept schema-ownership guidance within SchemaGrove screens instead of displaying a permanent notice across the WordPress site and network admin.
  • Restored the standard WordPress admin toolbar, footer, and active-menu styling while preserving the full-width SchemaGrove workspace.
  • Limited rare migration-failure notices to the Plugins screen using WordPress’s standard dismissible notice API.

1.0.7

  • Added the shared full-page template graph workspace used by SchemaGrove Pro, with draft-safe save-and-return behavior, dirty-change protection, responsive sizing, and accessible preview controls.
  • Added stable selected-property identifiers to graph extension actions so Pro canonical entities replace the intended property value and relationship instead of creating duplicates.
  • Removed stale canonical registry metadata when linked nodes are deleted and strengthened layered graph handling for canonical roots, overrides, and superseded entities.

1.0.6

  • Added a press-and-hold Option/Alt shortcut that temporarily switches the schema canvas between Grab and Pointer, restores the selected tool on release, and safely latches the active tool through an in-progress drag.
  • Kept Command/Ctrl-wheel canvas zoom and ordinary field input independent from the temporary tool shortcut, with safe recovery after focus or visibility changes.
  • Focused the Add Property search automatically whenever its picker opens, enabling immediate typing while preserving modal focus trapping and trigger-focus restoration.

1.0.5

  • Added first-class nested-schema creation for object-valued properties, including compatible type recommendations and an editable Entity ID child field.
  • Displayed arbitrary-depth entity, property, nested entity, and nested property relationships directly on the canvas with topology-aware auto-layout.
  • Preserved exact explicit nested entity IDs in local and server JSON-LD previews and removed stale relationship edges with deleted properties.
  • Kept nested-schema action text and icons white across interaction states and strengthened the Advanced-tab Remove property contrast.

1.0.4

  • Replaced the temporary geometric mark with the final SchemaGrove tree-and-circuit logo in the administrator header, setup wizard, and WordPress menu.
  • Added optimized transparent brand assets to the deterministic Lite release package.

1.0.3

  • Kept Site Audit severity icons and labels aligned inline for warning, error, success, unknown, and future status badges.
  • Scoped stacked finding details to their intended table column so they no longer override shared badge layout.

1.0.2

  • Made document-style administrator pages use natural page height and the main browser scrollbar instead of viewport-locked nested scrolling.
  • Expanded page headings and primary content frames to the available SchemaGrove workspace width for consistent alignment across tabs.
  • Removed secondary vertical scroll traps from long operational lists while preserving purpose-built canvas, dialog, preview, and responsive table scrolling.

1.0.1

  • Preserved manually positioned schema property cards when adding another property and placed new properties in deterministic collision-free canvas slots.
  • Made the Add property card movable and persistent across saves and reloads.
  • Added an explicit, deterministic, one-step-undoable Auto-organize graph action that changes layout without changing schema meaning.
  • Prevented older positionless property cards from jumping to the canvas origin after saving.

1.0.0

  • First production release of SchemaGrove Lite.
  • Added the complete visual Schema.org graph builder with content-aware starters, repeated properties, connected entity references, import/export, removal, replacement, validation, JSON-LD preview, and safe WordPress bindings.
  • Added responsive whole-site hierarchy, stored internal-link, schema-type, and entity-reference mapping in the pannable Site Graph.
  • Added public custom-post-type support, scalable content search, resource limits, granular capabilities, multisite-safe lifecycle handling, and an optional resumable setup wizard.
  • Added fail-closed schema ownership planning for sites using Yoast SEO, Rank Math, AIOSEO, SEOPress, WooCommerce, or another detected structured-data producer; third-party settings are never rewritten.
  • Bundled a reproducible, searchable full Schema.org catalog, human-readable source, pinned build dependencies, complete third-party notices, and deterministic release packaging.
